articles.title: ‘Standard’ velvet hangers? There’s nothing standard about some of the items on John Lewis’s uni essentials list| Emma Beddington
articles.summary: It used to be that dorm rooms were chaotically messy. Does this new generation really need an £80 spice rack and velvet clothes hangers? Of all the questions this year’s freshers may be nervously asking themselves as they prepare for this next phase – did I pick the right course?
body: Fret no longer, enquiring young minds: John Lewis has the answer on its packing checklist for students. Thirty to 40, it claims, wildly, “consisting mostly of standard velvet or plastic hangers”. “Standard” velvet? I missed this memo.

I found the list via the student news site the Tab, which posted a TikTok mocking J-Lew’s notions of what constitute “essentials”: a £495 Marc Jacobs bag, a £399 desk and an £80 spice rack carousel (I also spotted a £185 Ralph Lauren quarter-zip for those must-attend “man in finance” costume parties).

In fairness, most of the stuff on there is fine, but the Stanley cups and shower squeegees conjure a slightly dispiriting picture of wellness-focused, sensible, hygienic youth. I know that’s their generation’s reputation, but it would be nice if parents could be persuaded not to stock up, instead letting them go rogue and fill their kitchens, bathrooms and bedrooms with chaotically impractical stuff they choose themselves. Isn’t that what early adulthood is all about?
points: It used to be that dorm rooms were chaotically messy.
Does this new generation really need an £80 spice rack and velvet clothes hangers?

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Ernie the danger dog – who loves dicing with death
articles.summary: He has chased a deer across a dual carriageway, eaten an entire tray of chocolate brownies and jumped head first into a canal. But despite all the worry he brings us, he is extraordinarily lovable.
body: Ernie found his way into our hearts and home about nine years ago, when he strategically crawled into my lap during a family visit to meet a litter of puppies. While all the other beagle puppies ran wild, Ernie sat comfortably on me with his long, soft ears dangling down. We chose him because of his placid nature and named him Ernie after my mum’s late dad, who coincidentally also had short legs and a bit of a round belly.
After a few weeks we realised that Ernie was anything but placid. His gentle temperament quickly morphed into an unruly and persistent need to find his way into danger.

The most shocking incident happened one morning in November 2022. Ernie spotted a deer in the forest behind our house. He darted away from me and my mum, through the forest and towards a busy dual carriageway. Ignoring our screams, Ernie crossed the road, missing multiple lorries and cars, making his way to safety on a small patch of grass on the pavement. It was a miracle he had managed to avoid injury.
points: He has chased a deer across a dual carriageway, eaten an entire tray of chocolate brownies and jumped head first into a canal.
But despite all the worry he brings us, he is extraordinarily lovable.

articles.title: A job that changed me: I worked for an infamous clothing brand – but it was one of the most positive workplaces of my life
articles.summary: Despite its global reputation, my time there felt less sexy party, more wholesome summer camp. Then one day my boss told me a hard truth. When I tell people I spent a chunk of my early 20s working at a hipster clothing retailer infamous for salacious ads and sexual assault allegations, I’m usually…
body: But the truth is, despite the global reputation, our little store in Melbourne was one of the most positive workplaces of my life.

The store was divided into two tribes: shop assistants – mostly doe-eyed art girls – and backstock workers – mostly charming burnout skaters. While the shop assistants got the most attention and lustful public glares, the weed-scented heart of the store was the backstock room.
I was a rare breed: a shop assistant who transitioned to a backstock role, mostly because I couldn’t use a cash register properly.

Despite technically being a demotion, the move made me the envy of the shop assistants. In backstock we’d listen to music while folding T-shirts and debating Simpsons lore like greasy-haired scholars.
points: Despite its global reputation, my time there felt less sexy party, more wholesome summer camp.

articles.title: The Olaplex Shape Set Hairspray Wants You to Rethink Hold
articles.summary: The Olaplex Shape Set Hairspray is here—infusing its bond-repair technology into a hairspray that holds style sans crunch. Here's everything you need to know.
body: Olaplex launched 12 years ago with what was then a niche concept: products that not just superficially smooth and soften your hair, but actually repair broken bonds on a molecular level. As Amanda Baldwin, Olaplex CEO tells Vogue, “We’ve been the authority on hair health through bond-building with our patented technology, repairing the hair from the inside out.”

Fast forward to today the brand’s shampoos and conditioners, hair oils, hair masks, and more are flying off the shelf—while the bond repairing product business is utterly booming. What better time to introduce its next big hit? Behold: the Olaplex Shape Set Hairspray is here, and Vogue readers get exclusive access to shop it 24 hours early.

A product three years in the making, Olaplex saw a major opportunity to modernize the hairspray category entirely. “What’s interesting about hairspray is that it’s a category everyone knows, but a lot of people (particularly younger consumers) have almost opted out of it,” Baldwin adds. “There’s still this perception that hairspray means stiff, crunchy hair, or that you’re compromising the health of your hair to get the style you want.”
points: The Olaplex Shape Set Hairspray is here—infusing its bond-repair technology into a hairspray that holds style sans crunch.

articles.title: Michael Kors and Friends Toasted to the 45th Anniversary Collection Over Dinner in East Hampton
articles.summary: The Hamptons season may be winding down after a busy summer, but on Thursday evening, The Hedges Inn was still in full swing. Clad in Michael Kors Collection, a well-dressed crowd strolled down the hydrangea-lined brick path into the historic East Hampton hotel to lionize 45 years of the label and…
body: Guests swirled about in the garden of the 153-year-old property, which has been reimagined and revived by Sarah Wetenhall, who served as co-host for the soirée. Armed with tuna tartare-topped chips and glasses of local Wolffer Estate rosé, friends of the brand complimented each others’ sequined gowns and draped dresses while mingling in the courtyard. Katie Holmes posed with Kors near the bar, feting a friendship that spans decades. Naomi Watts, Molly Sims, and Sailor Brinkley Cook all fell into animated chatter as Aerin Lauder caught up with friends nearby.

As a few rain drops fell, signaling the end of the cocktail hour, the seated dinner party was soon underway. On the patio of Swifty’s, the fan-favorite on-site restaurant, two candlelit banquet tables beckoned. Varieties of white florals sat atop blue gingham tablecloths—a Hamptons-coded mise en place if there ever was.

articles.summary: Smart glass company RayNeo announced two new lines of smart glasses today: the minimal-display, AI-focused RayNeo iO, and the RayNeo GT and the GT Max, which are portable monitor glasses. They will all be available on Sept. 4 through RayNeo's site and on Amazon, but no prices were announced.
body: The company is aiming at two distinct segments of the smart glasses market with these models. The IO is productivity-minded, with a minimal monocular display, audio capability, and AI integration, where the GT series are tethered display glasses mainly for entertainment.
Lightweight frame designed for comfort. These glasses weigh only 33 grams, as light as an average pair of non-display glasses.

Integrated Ambient AI. Powered by Gemini's AI, RayNeo says their "Life Log" operates in the background and can "capture schedules and conversation contexts." It will extract action items and schedule calendar updates after meetings too.
Translation and teleprompter features: There's no audio, so translations and audio are all handled in the display.
